questions.question: In the absence of a formal partnership deed, how are profits and losses shared among partners according to the provisions of the Partnership Act?

options.A: In proportion to partners' capital contributions
options.C: In proportion to partners' total drawings
options.D: Based on years of service to the firm

questions.question: A and B are partners sharing profits in the ratio 3:2. They admit C as a new partner for a 1/5 share in profits. What is the new profit-sharing ratio among A, B, and C?
When a firm maintains fixed capital accounts, in which account is a partner's share of net profit, interest on capital, and drawings recorded?
Upon the admission of a new partner, goodwill is evaluated at ₦50,000, but the partners decide not to open a goodwill account in the financial books. What accounting entry records this adjustment?

options.A: Debit Goodwill Account ₦50,000; Credit Old Partners' Capital Accounts in old ratio ₦50,000
options.B: Debit All Partners' Capital Accounts in new ratio ₦50,000; Credit Goodwill Account ₦50,000
options.C: Debit New Partner's Capital Account; Credit Old Partners' Capital Accounts in sacrificing ratio
options.D: Debit Realization Account ₦50,000; Credit Bank Account ₦50,000

questions.question: Upon the dissolution of a partnership firm, where is the gain or loss resulting from the realization of assets and settlement of liabilities transferred?
Interest on a partner's loan to the firm, in the absence of an explicit agreement, is charged at what statutory rate per annum?

If total assets during a partnership dissolution realize ₦120,000, total external liabilities are ₦40,000, and dissolution expenses equal ₦5,000, what is the net realization surplus or deficit if book value of assets was ₦100,000?
Which component of share capital represents the maximum nominal value of shares a limited liability company is legally authorized to issue according to its Memorandum of Association?
When shares are issued at a premium, into which account is the excess amount received over the face value credited?
A company issues 10,000 ordinary shares of ₦1.00 each at ₦1.20. All application monies are received. What amount is credited to the Ordinary Share Capital account?
Which type of preference share entitles the holder to claim unpaid cumulative dividends from prior unprofitable years before any ordinary dividend is distributed?
When debentures are issued at a discount, how is the discount on issue of debentures presented on the financial statements until written off?

options.B: As a deduction from equity reserves or an asset/fictitious asset write-off item

questions.question: Where are proposed dividends and corporate taxation transfers recorded in a company's financial statements?

options.C: Profit and Loss Appropriation Account / Statement of Changes in Equity

questions.question: Which financial metric measures the proportion of earnings retained in the business relative to total profits generated after tax?
What is the primary characteristic of debentures compared to ordinary shares?

options.A: Debentures carry voting rights at Annual General Meetings
options.B: Debenture interest is a fixed charge against profit, regardless of profitability
options.C: Debenture holders receive variable dividends based on net earnings
options.D: Debentures form part of ownership equity

questions.question: Under single entry bookkeeping, how is net profit or loss calculated for a accounting period using the Statement of Affairs method?

options.A: Closing Capital + Drawings − Additional Capital Introduced − Opening Capital
options.B: Opening Capital + Drawings + Additional Capital Introduced − Closing Capital
options.C: Closing Capital − Drawings + Additional Capital Introduced − Opening Capital
options.D: Total Sales − Total Purchases − Operating Expenses

questions.question: A sole trader starts the year with assets of ₦80,000 and liabilities of ₦30,000. At the end of the year, assets are ₦110,000 and liabilities are ₦40,000. During the year, drawings were ₦15,000 and additional capital introduced was ₦5,000. What is the net profit?
In single entry accounting, how can total credit sales for the period be deduced when constructing a Total Debtors Account?

options.A: Closing Debtors + Cash Received from Debtors + Discounts Allowed − Opening Debtors
options.B: Opening Debtors + Cash Received from Debtors − Closing Debtors
options.C: Closing Debtors − Bad Debts Written Off − Opening Debtors
options.D: Opening Debtors + Total Receipts − Returns Outwards

questions.question: Given Opening Creditors ₦12,000, Payments to Creditors ₦45,000, Discount Received ₦2,000, and Closing Creditors ₦15,000, what is the value of total credit purchases?
A trader maintains a uniform markup of 25% on cost. If total sales for the period equal ₦100,000, what is the gross profit amount?
What primary financial statement is constructed in single entry systems to ascertain the capital position of a business at a specific date?
If a business has a margin of 20% on sales revenue and total cost of goods sold is ₦80,000, what is the total sales revenue?
In a manufacturing account, what items aggregate to constitute Prime Cost?

options.A: Direct Materials + Direct Labor + Direct Expenses

questions.question: Given: Opening Stock of Raw Materials ₦15,000, Purchases of Raw Materials ₦60,000, Carriage Inwards on Raw Materials ₦3,000, and Closing Stock of Raw Materials ₦12,000. What is the Cost of Raw Materials Consumed?
How are opening and closing stocks of Work-in-Progress (WIP) adjusted in a Manufacturing Account?

options.A: Opening WIP is added to, and Closing WIP is deducted from, overall manufacturing costs before arriving at production cost
options.B: Opening WIP is deducted from Prime Cost, and Closing WIP is added to Factory Overheads
options.C: Both Opening and Closing WIP are debited directly to the Trading Account
options.D: They are credited to the Profit and Loss Account as administrative income

questions.question: Which expense item is classified as a factory overhead rather than a prime cost element?

options.B: Direct wages of assembly line workers

questions.question: A firm manufactures goods at a total production cost of ₦200,000 and transfers them to the trading department at a market value of ₦230,000. How is the ₦30,000 manufacturing profit treated?

options.A: Debited to the Manufacturing Account and Credited to the Profit and Loss Account
options.B: Credited to the Trading Account as cost of goods sold
options.C: Deducted from closing finished goods inventory on the Balance Sheet
options.D: Debited directly to the Capital Account

questions.question: If Prime Cost is ₦140,000, Factory Overheads are ₦50,000, Opening Work-in-Progress is ₦10,000, and Closing Work-in-Progress is ₦15,000, what is the Production Cost of finished goods?
Where is the final cost of production transferred from the Manufacturing Account at the end of the financial period?

options.A: Debit side of the Trading Account
options.B: Credit side of the Profit and Loss Account
options.C: Asset side of the Balance Sheet
options.D: Credit side of the Manufacturing Profit Account

questions.question: When manufactured goods transferred to the trading department include a manufacturing profit, an adjustment for unrealized profit must be made against which inventory item at year-end?
